chapters.title: The Handshake Before the Meeting
chapters.tease: Buyers decide in a room you are not in. A book lets them meet you there before the call.

chapters.title: Brochures Are Read Once
chapters.tease: A brochure is about you and gets read once. A book is about the reader and gets kept.

chapters.title: Why One Hundred
chapters.tease: A hundred entries signals a body of work. The first thirty prove competence; the last seventy win the hire.

chapters.title: Generosity as Positioning
chapters.tease: Give the method away. Knowing what to do is not the same as getting it done, and buyers pay for the doing.

chapters.title: The Invisible Expert
chapters.tease: Expertise lives in your head, your calls and your emails. A book is the one layer a stranger can see.

chapters.title: Proof You Can Hold
chapters.tease: Proof that is specific and tangible beats claims. A book sits in the corner where little else does.

chapters.title: Format Lends, Content Keeps
chapters.tease: The book format lends you attention. Only useful content by page three turns it into trust you own.

chapters.title: What a Book Does to a Pipeline
chapters.tease: A book quietly removes friction from every stage of a sales pipeline, from first call to signature.

chapters.title: Who This Is For
chapters.tease: A book pays where clients buy judgement and each deal is big enough to be worth waiting for.

chapters.title: The Asset That Keeps Working
chapters.tease: Marketing activities stop when the budget does. A book is an asset that keeps working and compounds.

chapters.title: Narrow Enough to Be Chosen
chapters.tease: A book for everyone is recognised by no one. Narrow until ten real people would see themselves in it.

chapters.title: The Reader Is the Buyer
chapters.tease: Write for buyers, not peers. Speak to the manager with the problem and the director with the pen.

chapters.title: Writing the Promise Line
chapters.tease: One sentence that names a reader, a problem and an outcome. Every entry must serve that promise.

chapters.title: The Title Test
chapters.tease: A title has one job: make the right person pick the book up. Clever titles fail; clear ones work.

chapters.title: Ranked List or Hundred Chapters
chapters.tease: Choose the book's shape: a browsable Top 100, a hundred argued chapters, or a hybrid that does both.

chapters.title: The Angle Competitors Avoid
chapters.tease: Your angle lives in what your field privately agrees on and publicly avoids. Say it plainly.

chapters.title: The Problem Ladder
chapters.tease: Rank client problems from nice to fix up to hair on fire, and give the top rung most of the book.

chapters.title: Having a Point of View
chapters.tease: Information is free. A point of view, where experience meets opinion, is what buyers pay for.

chapters.title: Ten Entries Before a Hundred
chapters.tease: Write ten entries before a hundred. Show them to buyers and watch what they do, not what they say.

chapters.title: The One-Page Brief
chapters.tease: Fit every decision about the book on one page. It briefs every agent, designer, edit and reviewer.

chapters.title: You Already Know Ninety
chapters.tease: You do not lack a hundred ideas. You lack retrieval. Mine where your knowledge is already written down.

chapters.title: Mining the Sent Folder
chapters.tease: Your sent folder is a draft of your book, written for years to one reader at a time.

chapters.title: Client Questions Are Chapters
chapters.tease: Every question a client asks more than once is an entry. Let the market write your contents page.

chapters.title: Transcripts as Ore
chapters.tease: You speak better than you write. Mine recorded calls for strong answers, keep the voice, cut the clutter.

chapters.title: The Mistakes Inventory
chapters.tease: What goes wrong is the most valuable thing an expert knows. Turn every mistake into a four-layer entry.

chapters.title: Borrowing the Canon Carefully
chapters.tease: Use your field's classic frameworks, but credit them, apply them and add the twist only you can.

chapters.title: The Long List of Three Hundred
chapters.tease: Aim for three hundred candidates for a hundred-entry book. Quality comes from selection.

chapters.title: Culling to a Hundred
chapters.tease: Four passes take a long list to a hundred. The last asks: would you defend this to a sceptic?

chapters.title: Filling the Gaps
chapters.tease: Map your hundred against the buyer's journey. Readers notice where a book suddenly stops.

chapters.title: When the Well Runs Dry
chapters.tease: Stuck below a hundred? It is a message about scope. Read which cause fits, take its fix, never pad.

chapters.title: Ten by Ten
chapters.tease: Ten parts of ten entries turns a heap into a map readers can navigate and authors can plan.

chapters.title: Ranking Without Regret
chapters.tease: A ranked list is an argument. Rank by impact and urgency, state the principle once, and defend it.

chapters.title: From Ground Floor to Thesis
chapters.tease: Give a hundred-chapter book an arc: why it matters, how it works, what to do, then the thesis.

chapters.title: One Entry, One Lesson
chapters.tease: Every entry teaches one lesson a reader could use this week. Write that lesson as a sentence first.

chapters.title: The Entry Template
chapters.tease: Four movements give every entry a shape: lede, why, what to do, and a landing. The payoff is the what.

chapters.title: Openings That Earn the Next Line
chapters.tease: Readers decide in about a second whether to read line two. Open with a problem, a claim or a scene.

chapters.title: Landings, Not Summaries
chapters.tease: Do not end an entry by repeating it. Land it with a turn the reader can carry away.

chapters.title: Categories Readers Can Use
chapters.tease: Name parts like doors for what the reader is trying to do, not shelves labelled by the author.

chapters.title: Threads and Cross-References
chapters.tease: Three to five recurring threads turn a hundred tips into a book with a view.

chapters.title: The Last Entry States the Case
chapters.tease: Entry one hundred states the thesis plainly. Every earlier entry should be a step toward it.

chapters.title: The Factory, Not the Typewriter
chapters.tease: AI moved the bottleneck from typing to deciding. Run the book as a production line; editing is the payoff.

chapters.title: Brief Before Prompt
chapters.tease: Draft quality depends on context, not clever prompts. Give agents three layers: book, part and entry.

chapters.title: Capturing Your Voice
chapters.tease: The real risk in AI drafting is anonymity. A voice file of samples, rules and bans makes drafts yours.

chapters.title: One Part at a Time
chapters.tease: Draft one part at a time, edit it, then update the voice file. Each loop makes the next part faster.

chapters.title: The Outline Is the Contract
chapters.tease: Lock the outline before drafting: a forty-word line per entry is the contract every draft is checked against.

chapters.title: Agents Draft, You Decide
chapters.tease: Agents draft, you decide. Edit drafts with good bones; fix the input and redraft the rest.

chapters.title: Fact-Checking the Fluent
chapters.tease: Fluent is not the same as right. Check every confident claim: numbers, quotes, dates, laws and products.

chapters.title: Killing the Generic Sentence
chapters.tease: A generic sentence could sit in any book. Find them, cut the filler, rewrite the rest with specifics.

chapters.title: The QA Pass
chapters.tease: Editing checks judgement; a QA script checks mechanics. No pass, no ship.

chapters.title: Speed Is Not the Product
chapters.tease: Speed is not the product. Reinvest the time AI saves into care: the brief, the outline, the edit, the facts.

chapters.title: Looks Like a Book, Not a Deck
chapters.tease: Design the book like a book, not a deck. Book signals say knowledge; deck signals say pitch.

chapters.title: Brand Without Logo Soup
chapters.tease: Carry your brand through colour, type and tone, not logos. Recognised at a glance, promotional at none.

chapters.title: Typography Does the Work
chapters.tease: Body text is most of the book. Get its face, measure, leading and margins right and the book feels good.

chapters.title: One Diagram Per Entry
chapters.tease: One simple diagram per entry gives readers a second route back to every idea, and makes the book stick.

chapters.title: Choosing the Diagram
chapters.tease: A small set of diagram kinds covers nearly every idea. Match the kind to the shape the idea already has.

chapters.title: The Focal Node
chapters.tease: Every diagram gets one focal element in the accent colour: the payoff, never the input.

chapters.title: Labels You Can Read
chapters.tease: Short labels are a constraint that forces clarity. If it does not fit in the box, it is not yet the idea.

chapters.title: The Cover at Thumbnail Size
chapters.tease: Most people will only ever see your cover small. Design for the thumbnail first and the full size follows.

chapters.title: Light, Dark and Paper
chapters.tease: One design, expressed as named tokens, should work in light mode, dark mode, print and on a phone.

chapters.title: A System for Many Books
chapters.tease: Build the first book as a system of tokens, templates, data and engine, so the next book is mostly writing.

chapters.title: One Source, Many Outputs
chapters.tease: Keep the whole book in one structured source file and generate every edition from it.

chapters.title: The PDF Is the Workhorse
chapters.tease: The PDF is the edition that travels: attached, forwarded, saved and, at the moment of need, opened again.

chapters.title: Print as a Calling Card
chapters.tease: A printed book is a calling card: a physical object that represents you in rooms you are not in.

chapters.title: The Web Reader
chapters.tease: A web reader on your own domain gives every entry its own link, so the book can be found, not just opened.

chapters.title: The Swipeable App
chapters.tease: On a phone, the book should be a deck of cards: swipe, stop, save and, above all, come back.

chapters.title: The Email Course Edition
chapters.tease: Turn one part into ten plain emails that end by inviting a reply. The payoff is the conversation.

chapters.title: Talks From Chapters
chapters.tease: Each part is nearly the shape of a good talk. Cut it to three ideas and the book becomes the takeaway.

chapters.title: Cards and Clips
chapters.tease: Every entry is social content waiting to be released: a post, a card, a clip and a quote, all linking back.

chapters.title: Versions and Editions
chapters.tease: Date every edition and refresh it yearly. An undated book is a guess; a refreshed book is a promise kept.

chapters.title: Owning the Canonical Copy
chapters.tease: Spread the book widely, but keep one canonical copy on your own domain, and point everything there.

chapters.title: Launch to a Room, Not the World
chapters.tease: Launch to a room of fifty to two hundred named people, not the world. Books spread by recommendation.

chapters.title: The First Fifty Readers
chapters.tease: The first fifty readers set the book's reputation. Choose them from four groups and treat them as insiders.

chapters.title: Gated or Free
chapters.tease: Keep the web reader open for discovery; ask for an email only in exchange for the PDF or course.

chapters.title: The Landing Page
chapters.tease: A landing page answers three questions, what is it, is it for me, what do I do now, then offers one button.

chapters.title: Sending It Personally
chapters.tease: Send the book personally, one note at a time, naming an entry chosen for that person. People answer doors.

chapters.title: One Entry a Day
chapters.tease: Serialise the book on one channel. Post, listen to who leans in, then adjust the next post and edition.

chapters.title: Borrowed Audiences
chapters.tease: Borrow other people's audiences where they overlap your buyers. The book is your invitation to their room.

chapters.title: Partners Who Pass It On
chapters.tease: Partners who serve your buyers without competing can pass the book on, and their trust arrives with it.

chapters.title: Marketplaces and Shelves
chapters.tease: List on marketplaces once, properly, for credibility. Then put your launch energy elsewhere.

chapters.title: The Long Tail of a Launch
chapters.tease: Launch week is the least important part of the book's life. The value builds over months and years.

chapters.title: Send the Book Before the Call
chapters.tease: Send two or three chosen entries before the first call, so the call starts on their situation.

chapters.title: The Spec Sample
chapters.tease: A spec sample is ten entries written for one prospect's world. It shows rather than tells what you would do.

chapters.title: Talking Through Entry Twelve
chapters.tease: Once a prospect has read an entry, it becomes scaffolding for the call: agenda, example, answer and next step.

chapters.title: Objections Already Answered
chapters.tease: Write a calm, honest entry for each common objection, then point to it on calls instead of defending live.

chapters.title: Leave-Behinds That Get Opened
chapters.tease: Follow up with the three entries you discussed, a short note on their case, the book and your details.

chapters.title: The Follow-Up Ladder
chapters.tease: Bridge the gap between a free book and a full engagement with a small, paid middle rung.

chapters.title: Workshops, Audits and Retainers
chapters.tease: Your book is a product catalogue in disguise: audits, workshops, retainers and talks all grow from it.

chapters.title: Measuring Whether It Pays
chapters.tease: Judge the book by whether it helps win valuable clients. Ask every client how they found you.

chapters.title: Leading Indicators
chapters.tease: Track four weekly numbers, sent, calls, proposals and clients, to see early whether the book is working.

chapters.title: Keep, Refresh or Kill
chapters.tease: Decide on evidence, by dates set at launch. Refresh is usually right; prices are never the first lever.

chapters.title: Doing It for Clients
chapters.tease: The method that produced your book can produce your clients'. They buy a finished asset, not words.

chapters.title: The Intake Interview
chapters.tease: A ninety-minute intake interview supplies most of a client book. The hard questions supply the best entries.

chapters.title: Fixed Scope, Fixed Calendar
chapters.tease: Productise the book service: a fixed scope and a fixed calendar, the same for every client.

chapters.title: The Client's Voice, Not Yours
chapters.tease: A client book must sound like the client. Their words and knowledge, shaped by your craft.

chapters.title: Partners and White Label
chapters.tease: Partners who serve experts can sell your book service. Choose them by fit and supply, like a co-author.

chapters.title: The Refresh Habit
chapters.tease: A book delivered is not a book finished. Collect notes, refresh on schedule and relaunch every year.

chapters.title: Many Books Without Chaos
chapters.tease: Producing many books is an operation. Shared engine, a folder per book and a tracker give calm delivery.

chapters.title: Honest About the Machine
chapters.tease: Say plainly that AI helped draft the book, and that the knowledge, judgement and final text are the author's.

chapters.title: What the Book Cannot Do
chapters.tease: A book cannot fix an offer, deliver, sell itself or make you an expert. What it can do is open the door.

chapters.title: The Book Is the Handshake
chapters.tease: The whole book in one line: write what you know, put it where buyers look, and arrive already known.
